# EvTab

> One tab in a Tabs strip; its value selects it, and it takes the variant from the Tabs around it.

| ID | `evoq-ui:tab` |
| Layer | Atom (`src/atoms`) |

| Extra attributes go to | the root `<button class="ev-tab">` |
| Used inside | `evoq-ui:tabs` (EvTabs) |

## Design guidance

From the Figma page **Tabs**, frame `4100:63234` (Tabs). These rules are binding. Names in them are Figma's - the Vue API is the tables above.

### When to use

- Use to switch between related views or sections within one page or panel.
- Use when content is peer-level and only one view shows at a time.
- Use the segmented style for a small, fixed set of toggles or filters.
- Use the line style for primary, section-level navigation.

### When not to use

- Don't use for sequential steps  →  use a Stepper
- Don't use for page-to-page navigation  →  use a Nav menu (`evoq-ui:navigation-menu`)
- Don't use to filter many options  →  use Select / Chips
- Don't use when views are unrelated or hierarchical.

### Do

- Keep exactly one tab selected at all times
- Keep labels short (1–2 words) and parallel
- Keep the visible panel in sync with the active tab
- Limit the count so all tabs fit without scrolling

### Don't

- Open a new page or dialog from a tab
- Hide critical content behind a rarely-seen tab
- Use long labels that wrap or truncate
- Nest tabs inside tabs in the same view

## Contract

- Only the props, slots and events above exist on `EvTab`; anything not listed is not part of its API.
- An attribute that is not a prop (`class`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) goes to the root `<button class="ev-tab">`.
- Import it by name from `evoq-ui`; styles come once from `evoq-ui/style.css`.
- Refer to it by id `evoq-ui:tab` - the id stays the same if the component moves layer.
